item.title: India to Announce Banking Review Committee Soon, Sitharaman Says
item.description: India is set to soon announce a high-powered committee to recommend how the banking sector should evolve to support the country’s transformation into a developed economy within the next two decades, the finance minister said Monday.

item.title: Indian Lenders Set Record With $8 Billion in Dollar Bond Sales
item.description: Indian financial institutions have sold a record amount of dollar bonds so far this year, as lenders rush to capitalize on a central bank facility that lowers hedging costs on overseas borrowings.

item.title: Asian Refiners Ask to Pick Up Saudi Oil Outside Risky Red Sea
item.description: Some Asian refiners are pushing back against Saudi Aramco’s request that they pick up their oil at Yanbu on the Red Sea, due to the difficulty of finding ships willing to sail through the dangerous waterway.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: Futures Rise as Stocks Globally Rally
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: Futures Rise as Stocks Globally Rally【原文：FTSE 100 Live: Futures Rise as Stocks Globally Rally】

item.title: Emerging Currencies Rise to Record High as Fed Hike Bets Ease
item.description: Emerging-market currencies rose to a record high as bets on a Federal Reserve interest rate hike cooled, spurring demand for risk assets.

item.title: South Africa to Finalize Rules for $9.3 Trillion OTC Derivatives Market by 2028
item.description: South Africa’s financial regulators plan to finalize new rules requiring over-the-counter derivatives to be centrally cleared in the next two years to improve transparency and reduce risk.

item.title: AI Era Demands More Agile Leaders, Harvard’s Linda Hill Says
item.description: The next generation of chief executives will need to spend more time building flexible organizations as the deployment of artificial intelligence rapidly reshapes how companies do business, according to Harvard Business School Professor Linda Hill.

item.title: India Short-Tenor Bond Yields Climb on Early Dollar Window Close
item.description: Shorter-tenor India bond yields surged after the central bank said it will close a special dollar deposit window for overseas residents a month earlier than scheduled.

item.title: UAE’s L’imad Offers to Delist AD Ports at $8.66 Billion Value
item.description: Abu Dhabi wealth fund L’imad Holding is offering to buy out minority shareholders in the city’s port operator valuing the firm at 31.8 billion dirhams ($8.66 billion), in a move that could reverse the emirate’s recent push to bring more strategic holdings to public markets.

item.title: Sembcorp Said to Plan Filing for $500 Million IPO of India Unit
item.description: Singapore-based Sembcorp Industries Ltd. is preparing to file for an initial public offering of its Indian unit, Sembcorp Green Infra Ltd., that could raise as much as $500 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: First Gen Falls by Record 19% After Parent Rejected KKR Offer
item.description: Shares of First Gen Corp., one of the Philippines’ largest renewable energy companies, fell by a record on Monday after its parent turned down an offer from KKR to buy additional shares and take it private.

item.title: Goldman Says Markets Too Hawkish on Betting Fed Will Hike Rates
item.description: Market bets on Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes are still too aggressive given that inflation in the world’s biggest economy is cooling, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc.

item.title: BOJ Should Raise Rates at Every Meeting, Ex-Currency Chief Says
item.description: The Bank of Japan should raise its benchmark interest rate at every meeting, with the goal of taking the rate above 2% in order to narrow the rate differential with the US and ease pressure on the yen, a former Finance Ministry official said.

item.title: Korea Eximbank to Lend $1 Billion to Glencore for Copper Supply
item.description: Export-Import Bank of Korea will lend $1 billion to commodities giant Glencore Plc in exchange for copper supply to South Korean companies, as the country seeks to secure raw materials needed for the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Indonesian Developer Modernland Seeks Bond Restructuring Again
item.description: Distressed Indonesian property firm PT Modernland Realty is seeking to restructure a dollar bond for a second time, highlighting liquidity challenges facing the builder of residential and industrial townships.

item.title: Japan’s Bond Yields Climb on BOJ Hike Bets, Fiscal Concerns
item.description: Japan’s bonds fell on fiscal concerns and growing speculation that the Bank of Japan may raise interest rates in the coming months, pushing the 10-year yield to the highest since 1996.

item.title: India Rupee, Bonds in Focus as RBI to End FCNR Deposit Window Early
item.description: The end of the deposit plan could tighten banking system liquidity.

item.title: Thai Growth Slows to 1.9% as Energy Prices Counter Stimulus
item.description: Thailand’s economic growth slowed dramatically in the second quarter, lagging its Southeast Asian peers, as higher energy prices countered stronger investment and government stimulus.

item.title: Xi Touts Party-Led Growth at Predecessor’s Birth Centenary
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping upheld former leader Jiang Zemin’s legacy of combining economic development with firm Communist Party rule, using the centenary of his predecessor’s birth to reinforce the political foundations of his own agenda.

item.title: Hong Kong Court Orders Unit of SDIC Commodities to Liquidate
item.description: A unit of China’s state-backed SDIC Commodities Co. was ordered to liquidate by a Hong Kong court, adding to the financial troubles for the metals trader as Beijing increases scrutiny on the sector.

item.title: Silver Traders Brave Red Tape to Capture Indian Premiums
item.description: Shipments of silver into India are picking up despite administrative hurdles, as traders seek to capitalize on attractive premiums after a new licensing regime disrupted imports.

item.title: Copper Heads Toward Record High on LME as Supply Tensions Build
item.description: Copper extended a seven-week rally to head toward a record, with a key price spread on the London Metal Exchange widening to unusual levels in a clear sign of rising competition for short-term supply.

item.title: Sri Lankan Inflation to Slow Toward Goal, Central Bank Head Says
item.description: Sri Lanka’s inflation is expected to slow back toward the central bank’s target of 5% over the second half of this year and into next year, according to Governor Nandalal Weerasinghe.

item.title: CXMT’s Rise to China’s Most Valuable Firm Heralds New Tech Era
item.description: CXMT Corp.’s ascent to the pinnacle of Chinese markets heralds a potentially consequential shift away from private-sector giants toward a new generation of hardware companies more closely aligned with Beijing’s strategic ambitions.

item.title: Alibaba to Sell Gaming Arm for $1.5 Billion in Boost to AI Pivot
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. is selling its gaming arm in a deal worth at least $1.5 billion that will boost the Chinese e-commerce leader’s pivot to AI.

item.title: Alphabet Hires Banks for Inaugural Aussie Dollar Bond Sale
item.description: Alphabet Inc. hired banks for what would be a debut offering of Australian dollar bonds, as US tech firms flood credit markets with debt to fund investments in AI.

item.title: Thai Baht Rally May Fade on Dovish Central Bank, Analysts Say
item.description: A nascent rally in the Thai baht may be short-lived as the central bank is likely to maintain a dovish policy stance to support an economy hit by elevated oil prices, according to analysts.

item.title: Japanese Idol App Firm Collapses Amid Wave of Bankruptcies
item.description: A Japanese company known for a game app based around virtual teen idols filed for bankruptcy, the latest in a wave of corporate failures that climbed to the most in 12 years as inflation and worker shortages hit weaker firms.

item.title: Japan’s Slower Growth Complicates BOJ’s Messaging on Rate Hike
item.description: Japan’s economic growth unexpectedly slowed in the three months through June, a result that may complicate the Bank of Japan’s policy communications as it weighs the timing of its next rate increase.

item.title: Gold Steady Near $4,400 as Traders Weigh US Data and Rate Path
item.description: Gold was steady as traders weighed the competing impacts of cooling US economic data and energy-led inflation pressure on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.
